To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-4 synergistically enhances IL-12-induced NK cell proliferation.
the combination of IL4 and IL-2 induces synergistic proliferative responses in CD56+NK cells.
IL-4 and interleukine 12 synergistically stimulate the proliferative response of NK cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synergistic effect of IL-12 andIL-4 on the proliferation and activation of CD56+, CD3-, CD16+ NK cells, which are important in the generation of LAK cells.
the development of new strategies for the treatment of cancer, based on the use of IL-4 as a costimulant of IL-12-induced CD56+ NK cell activation.
the identification of the optimal cytokine combination for NK cell activation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of IL4 and IL-7 is the best for the induction of NK cell proliferation and the combination of IL12 and IL7 is the best combination for the induction of LAK activity.
IL-12 and/or IL-12 plus IL-4 may be useful in the generation of large quantities of activated NK cells for clinical applications.
the combination of IL12 and IL-12 and/or IL-12 and is a promising candidate for the development of CD56+ and/or IL-7.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-4 and the IL-12/IL-12R system are involved in the regulation of NK cell proliferation and activation.

IL-12 and/or IL-4 may have a potential role in the treatment of cancer, as the combination of IL12 and IL-7 or IL-4 and/or IL-12 can be used to generate high LAF activity and high proliferative activity in the CD56- cells.
IL-4 is a potent costimulus to IL-12 for the proliferation of resting CD56+ cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of IL4 and IL-2 or IL-12 may provide an efficient and potent in vivo activation of NK cells, which may be useful in the treatment of cancer and viral diseases.
the synergistic effect of IL-12 andIL-4 on NK cell activation may be a useful strategy to enhance the therapeutic effect of NK cell immunotherapy in cancer patients.
IL-4 can synergize with IL-12 to induce a potent proliferative response and increase in cell number in the NK cell population.
